current.text: He looks set to start for Washington. The newest note says he is almost locked in to start over Bilal Coulibaly.
He had three blocks in his last preseason game.
Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, who will take most of the shots and touches.
Experts expect him to be about the fifth offensive option. They do not think he repeats last season's production, when he started as a top 50 player with a bigger ball handling role before he faded.
Experts rate him a late round pick. One calls his ADP of 112 marginally high.
One analyst sees him as the organization's favorite and the best all-around player among Washington's young wings and guards.
Washington has a deep group of wings and expects a 10 or 11 man rotation, so minutes are spread.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so the late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not happen.

durable.text: Two-way wing who can guard shooting guard through power forward but can struggle against quicker guards. He shoots well from outside, mostly on catch-and-shoot chances.
His blocks are strong for his position.
An arm injury ended his 2025-26 season early.

note: He is ranked 120 on Yahoo and 129 on ESPN, worth 1 USD on both. He went for 2 USD in our league last season. That puts him near the edge of our 144-player pool, so treat him as a 1 to 2 USD end-of-draft wing for blocks, threes and some assists. Do not pay more, because his projected 43% FG on about 11 shots and 2.3 turnovers cost you. Early in the season, check that he keeps the starting spot over Coulibaly and how many shots he gets next to Young, Davis and Dybantsa. If he falls to bench minutes, he is a waiver-level player.
